# LegacyShell Wiki

> LegacyShell is a from-scratch reimplementation of the backend and client for the browser game Shell Shockers (shellshock.io) at version 0.17.0, plus original extensions (a commands system, new gamemodes, an in-game map editor, a plugin API). This file indexes the documentation wiki for humans and AI agents; see https://github.com/onlypuppy7/LegacyShell for the source. The complete text of every page below is concatenated at /llms-full.txt.

## Documentation

- [Documentation Home](/wiki/docs/): Router page - start here to find the right section for what you're trying to do.

### Getting Started

- [Getting Started](/wiki/docs/01-Getting%20Started/): This section gets you from "never heard of LegacyShell" to a running local server with your own admin account. It assumes nothing about your technical background.
- [Config Files](/wiki/docs/01-Getting%20Started/config-files.html): Two folders matter:
- [First Run](/wiki/docs/01-Getting%20Started/first-run.html): The simplest way to run LegacyShell is one command that starts all three servers at once:

- [Making an Account](/wiki/docs/01-Getting%20Started/making-an-account.html): Playing as a guest works fine, but an account is what gets you persistent stats, an inventory, and the ability to be granted admin.
- [Requirements](/wiki/docs/01-Getting%20Started/requirements.html): LegacyShell is a Node.js project - you need Node installed to run any of it. There's no strict minimum version pinned in the project itself, but these versions are known to work in practice (from t...
- [Speed Setup](/wiki/docs/01-Getting%20Started/speed-setup.html): The whole thing, four commands. Every one of them is explained in far more depth on the pages that follow this one - come back to those if something here doesn't make sense, doesn't match what you...
- [Troubleshooting (Getting Started)](/wiki/docs/01-Getting%20Started/troubleshooting.html): Problems specific to first-time setup. For issues once you're actually operating a server day to day, see Running a Server troubleshooting instead.
- [What is LegacyShell?](/wiki/docs/01-Getting%20Started/what-is-legacyshell.html): LegacyShell is a from-scratch, open-source rebuild of the backend and browser client for Shell Shockers (shellshock.io), an egg-themed multiplayer shooter, preserved as it played at version 0.17.0...

### Running a Server

- [Running a Server](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/): This section covers actually operating a LegacyShell deployment: the database, user ranks, connecting multiple game servers, keeping it alive unattended, and moderating it once it's public.
- [Adding Game Servers](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/adding-game-servers.html): A game server won't do anything useful - won't show up in the server list, can't record kills, can't fetch account data - until it's authorized by the services server it's syncing with. Authorizati...
- [Architecture Overview](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/architecture-overview.html): What is LegacyShell? introduced the three servers at a glance. This page goes one level deeper - what you actually need to know to operate a real deployment, especially once it's more than "everyth...
- [Backups](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/backups.html): Services backs up its own SQLite database automatically - no separate tooling needed, but worth understanding exactly what it does and doesn't protect against.
- [Client Mirrors](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/client-mirrors.html): Unlike a game server (which needs authorization), a client server needs no registration at all - anyone can stand one up pointed at your services server, the same way anyone can run a mirror of a n...
- [Closed Mode](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/closed-mode.html): There are two separate "closed" switches in LegacyShell, easy to confuse, that do genuinely different things.
- [Deployment](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/deployment.html): Running LegacyShell somewhere reachable from the internet, rather than just localhost. This page covers the parts specific to LegacyShell; general server-hardening practice (firewalls, SSH keys, un...
- [Hosting for Someone Else's Instance](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/hosting-for-another-instance.html): Adding Game Servers and Client Mirrors are written for the person who owns the whole deployment - they assume you have filesystem access to LegacyShellData.db and are adding capacity to your own in...
- [Moderation](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/moderation.html): Practical, day-to-day moderation - what commands actually exist, and what to reach for when something goes wrong in a room.
- [Perpetual](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/perpetual.html): Every npm run client/services/game command runs through Perpetual - a process-supervisor wrapper that keeps a server alive unattended: auto-restart on crash, a daily restart schedule, automatic git...
- [Rate Limiting](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/rate-limiting.html): Services rate-limits incoming WebSocket commands per-IP, to keep a single misbehaving or malicious client from hammering the database or auth flow.
- [The Database](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/the-database.html): Everything persistent in LegacyShell - accounts, stats, inventories, maps, items, redemption codes, authorized game servers - lives in one SQLite file: server-services/store/LegacyShellData.db. Onl...
- [Troubleshooting (Running a Server)](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/troubleshooting.html): Operational problems once you're past initial setup - for first-install issues, see Getting Started troubleshooting instead.
- [Users and Ranks](/wiki/docs/02-Running%20a%20Server/users-and-ranks.html): Every account has an adminRoles integer column in the users table (default 0). That number is compared against named rank levels defined in store/config/distributed_permissions.yaml:

- [Gamemodes](/wiki/docs/03-Content%20Creation/gamemodes.html): What you can configure about gamemodes without writing any code - creating a genuinely new gamemode is a coding task, covered in Plugin Development instead.
- [Hats and Stamps](/wiki/docs/03-Content%20Creation/hats-and-stamps.html): Hats and stamps both use the general item shape (item_type_id 1 and 2 respectively) - a hat is just another 3D model like a weapon skin (see Dealing with Babylon Models). Stamps are the one genuine...
- [Items and Skins](/wiki/docs/03-Content%20Creation/items-and-skins.html): Adding a new weapon skin, hat, or stamp to the shop - the catalog/inventory system, not to be confused with pickup items (ammo/grenades/health packs, a completely separate in-world-collectible syst...
- [Map Blocks](/wiki/docs/03-Content%20Creation/map-blocks.html): Adding a new placeable, collidable block type to the map editor - distinct from Maps (arranging existing blocks into a map) and general model work (this page is specifically about the naming conven...
- [Maps](/wiki/docs/03-Content%20Creation/maps.html): Building and installing a custom map - no coding required, using the in-game map editor.
- [Seasonal Events](/wiki/docs/03-Content%20Creation/seasonal-events.html): How the shop's seasonal rotation actually decides what's available, and what you can hook into as a content creator without touching gameplay code.
- [Sounds](/wiki/docs/03-Content%20Creation/sounds.html): LegacyShell replaced the original game's audio with its own Howler.js-based wrapper, Apollo - see Sound and Apollo for the API a plugin uses to register and play sounds in code; this page covers ad...

- [Codebase Anecdotes](/wiki/docs/05-Codebase%20Reference/anecdotes.html): Known Quirks is the "this could actually bite you" page. This one isn't - it's just the personality of the source: a maintainer talking to themselves, to future readers, and occasionally to the cod...
- [Build Pipeline](/wiki/docs/05-Codebase%20Reference/build-pipeline.html): How src/client-static/src/shellshock.min.js (the hand-maintained, not actually minified browser game source) becomes the real, served, minified bundle in store/client-modified/.
- [Catalog and Items](/wiki/docs/05-Codebase%20Reference/catalog-and-items.html): The engineering detail underneath the catalog/shop system - item ID encoding and the weekly shop-rotation algorithm. For the content-creator-facing item shape, see Items and Skins.
- [Game Loop](/wiki/docs/05-Codebase%20Reference/game-loop.html): The authoritative 60Hz simulation loop every room runs, and the reconciliation mechanism that keeps client prediction honest.
- [Wire Protocol Opcodes](/wiki/docs/05-Codebase%20Reference/Generated/comm-opcodes.html): Every entry in Comm.Code (src/shell/comm.js), extracted directly from source, along with its JSDoc comment where one exists. See Networking for how to register your own opcode with Comm.Add.
- [Config Reference](/wiki/docs/05-Codebase%20Reference/Generated/config-reference.html): Every key in every src/defaultconfig/.yaml template, with its default value and the comment(s) written above/beside it in source - extracted directly, not hand-maintained. Your actual settings live...
- [Database Schema](/wiki/docs/05-Codebase%20Reference/Generated/database-schema.html): Every CREATE TABLE statement in server-services/src/data_management/recordsManagement.js, extracted directly from source. This is the literal DDL LegacyShell runs on boot - for the editability tags...
- [Enums & Lookup Tables](/wiki/docs/05-Codebase%20Reference/Generated/enums-reference.html): Every top-level, flat, all-number-valued object literal in src/shell/constants.js and src/shell/comm.js, extracted directly from source - whether or not it carries a JSDoc @enum tag (most of the re...
- [Slash Command Reference](/wiki/docs/05-Codebase%20Reference/Generated/slash-commands.html): Every built-in this.newCommand({...}) call in src/shell/permissions.js, extracted directly from source. Plugin-registered commands aren't included here since they don't exist until a plugin loads -...

## Plugins

- [Plugins Section](/wiki/plugins/): This is a section reserved for info about plugins.
- [List of plugins](/wiki/plugins/listofplugins.html): Here is a list of known plugins for LegacyShell. (You may even notice a pattern with who made them!)

### Plugins - Default

- [Crackshot](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/5_crackshot/info.html): Adds Crackshot, the 0.20.0-era bolt-action sniper rifle (internally the M24 weapon class), as a brand new primary-weapon slot rather than reskinning an existing one - it registers its own CharClass...
- [Auto Restart Notifications](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/autorestartnotifications/info.html): Warns players in-room before a scheduled daily server restart, at nine fixed checkpoints: 30, 15, 10, 5, and 1 minute before, then 30, 10, and 5 seconds before, and finally "Server is restarting no...
- [Auto Shop Notifications](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/autoshopnotifications/info.html): Posts the weekly shop rotation to a Discord webhook once a week, as soon as a new rotation is computed - a public-facing message (item names/prices/tiers) and a separate, more detailed "dev" messag...
- [Burnt Block Sets](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/burntblocksets/info.html): Replaces the entire base map model set with a custom block set contributed by Burnt Apple - every map block, reskinned and/or reshaped at once, rather than adding new blocks alongside the defaults.
- [Christmas Event](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/christmasevent/info.html): A seasonal content plugin: adds Christmas-themed models (a gift box, mistletoe, baubles, stockings, wreaths, gingerbread, candy canes, snowy tree variants), swaps certain map blocks for snowy versi...
- [DeadInternet](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/deadinternet/info.html): Adds bot players to your game. As of this version, DeadInternet also ships a general-purpose A\ pathfinding engine over the game's real voxel collision grid, so bots (or any other plugin) can navig...
- [FancyGraphics](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/fancygraphics/info.html): A small "readds old/nicer visual options" plugin - adds an optional fancy-shadows mode (hands and gun meshes cast shadows, not just the player body), an outline effect on fired bullets, and a littl...
- [Health Pack Item](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/healthpackitem/info.html): Adds a Health Pack pickup item that heals the collecting player 50 HP, using the game:AllItems extension point - the same mechanism documented generically in Recipe: New Pickup Item, from the plugi...
- [Item ToolTips](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/itemtooltips/info.html): Adds a hover tooltip showing an item's name when hovering over its tile in the shop UI - a small, self-contained UI enhancement.
- [LegacyAnalytics](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/legacyanalytics/info.html): A services-side analytics plugin: logs gameplay/account activity into its own separate SQLite database (not LegacyShellData.db), and serves a small built-in web dashboard to chart it.
- [LegacySettings](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/legacysettings/info.html): A complete replacement settings-menu UI, and - more importantly for other plugin authors - a small framework other plugins build their own settings tabs on top of. FancyGraphics is a real example o...
- [LegacyShellCore](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/legacyshellcore/info.html): The flagship content-pack plugin - custom maps, items, stamps, a baseline shop pool, and a couple of gameplay easter eggs, all bundled together. Referenced throughout the rest of this wiki as the c...
- [LegacyThemes](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/legacythemes/info.html): A CSS theme-switching framework, parallel to Legacy Settings - lets a player stack multiple named "style packs" (each just a CSS file plus some metadata) on top of the base theme, reorderable and r...
- [Modern Map Blocks](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/modernmapblocks/info.html): Re-adds newer (post-0.17.0) Shell Shockers map block models - purely a model/content pack, no gameplay logic of its own.
- [Modern Shell Guns](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/modernshellguns/info.html): Re-adds newer (post-0.17.0) Shell Shockers gun models and their items, alongside the legacy 0.17.0-era weapons rather than replacing them.
- [Modern Shell Hats](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/modernshellhats/info.html): Re-adds newer (post-0.17.0) Shell Shockers hat models and their items, additively.
- [Modern Shell Stamps](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/modernshellstamps/info.html): Re-adds newer (post-0.17.0) Shell Shockers stamps.
- [Minerva](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/multiplayermaphost/info.html): Internally identified as "Minerva" (PluginMeta.name, distinct from its folder/identifier multiplayermaphost) - lets the in-editor map maker test a map in a real, live multiplayer match instead of t...
- [ParkourMode](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/parkourmode/info.html): Adds a full "Parkour" gamemode - checkpoints, a goal, sound cues, and egg rewards - built entirely on ordinary plugin extension points, no core engine changes.
- [Player Count Notifications](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/playercountnotifications/info.html): Posts the current player count to a Discord webhook on a timer, tracking each day's highest public/private/total counts along the way. Game-server-only (plugins.type !== "game" skips everything else).
- [TimeMachine](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/timemachine/info.html): A "throwback options" plugin - lets a player opt back into older (pre-0.17.0) visual behavior: bullet holes (removed in 0.17.0, this plugin reimplements the 0.9.0 and 0.1.0 versions), bullet smoke,...
- [Vaporwave Map Blocks](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/vaporwaveblocks/info.html): Adds a full vaporwave-styled map block set, plus its own maps built around that block set - a content pack in the same family as Burnt Block Sets, but shipping matching maps alongside the blocks ra...
- [WhatsAppTheme](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/whatsapptheme/info.html): An intentionally silly example theme - re-skins LegacyShell to look like WhatsApp. Its own description says as much: "An example theme made by onlypuppy7."
- [Zaxonius Custom Guns](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Default/zaxoniuscustomguns/info.html): Swaps in an alternate Crackshot model set contributed by Zaxonius, reusing the 5_crackshot plugin's weapon slot and logic rather than defining a new weapon.

### Plugins - Examples

- [Modern Shell Maps](/wiki/plugins/Plugin%20Docs/Examples/modernshellmaps/info.html): Re-adds Shell Shockers' modern-era map pool (plus their Halloween/Christmas texture variants), which isn't part of LegacyShell's classic-era default map set.

## Wiki

- [Wiki Home](/wiki/wiki/): Shell Shockers lore, history, and trivia - not part of /llms-full.txt.
